workItem.title: Bridge-readiness: public proof-status oracle IAU candidate

publicContinuityEvidence.role: public Windows Docker Desktop Windows-container proof intake signal

excludedBehavior: Docker command execution or container orchestration
new Windows Docker Desktop proof admission without real Windows Docker Desktop evidence
source copying from another product line

comparisonResults.topic: Linux host proof remains distinct from Windows proof
comparisonResults.expectedGovernedBehavior: Linux host LabVIEW proof is admitted evidence but must not masquerade as Windows proof or Windows Docker Desktop proof.
comparisonResults.observedMitBehavior: T026 creates Linux host proof packets and validates that they are not accepted as Windows Docker Desktop proof.

comparisonResults.expectedGovernedBehavior: The public validation lane exposes a canonical validate-fixture proof packet with structured JSON and deterministic issue-body content.
comparisonResults.observedMitBehavior: T028 and T029 create proof packets and deterministic issue bodies from retained runtime, execution, report, host, Docker Desktop, and fixture facts.

comparisonResults.expectedGovernedBehavior: Windows Docker Desktop proof requires real Windows host facts, Docker Desktop OSType windows, canonical fixture command, successful execution, and generated-report evidence.
comparisonResults.observedMitBehavior: T027 rejects Linux Docker, WSL, host-provider proof, and reports without proof packets; T030 accepts only packets with the required Windows Docker Desktop Windows-container facts.

comparisonResults.expectedGovernedBehavior: Proof intake validation does not run LabVIEWCLI, orchestrate Docker, admit new Windows Docker Desktop proof, mutate Marketplace state, or copy source from another authority.
comparisonResults.observedMitBehavior: The MIT implementation is pure data-contract validation and artifact rendering. No command execution, Docker orchestration, Marketplace behavior, or source-copying surface was added.

bugOracleClassification.rationale: The governed proof-status requirements, public Spec Kit runtime-contract feature, and MIT clean-room proof-intake implementation agree for T026 through T030. No new public import or implementation IAU is needed because the candidate is already covered by the existing runtime-contract bridge.

nextGovernedAction.reason: After proof-status/oracle scope is closed through the existing runtime-contract import and oracle review, the next remaining non-blocked candidate is the command activation surface.
